status.en: 180 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 32% fewer than the week before, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Plateau State.
status.nb: 180 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 32 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Plateau State.

summary.en: Armed incidents have fallen 20% over the past week, with 211 reports concentrated in Abuja, Lagos and Plateau State, and 24 involving multiple outlets. Battle‑related deaths in 2024 total 1,486. Violence continues in Plateau, where gunmen have killed miners and a police officer, and attacks on herders have left dozens dead in Benue and other states. Kidnappings and human‑trafficking rescues are also reported, while the government pledges to rescue abducted children in Borno.
summary.nb: Væpnede hendelser har falt 20 % den siste uken, med 211 rapporter konsentrert i Abuja, Lagos og Plateau State, og 24 som involverte flere medier. Kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024 er 1 486. Volden fortsetter i Plateau, hvor væpnede har drept gruvearbeidere og en politimann, og angrep på hyrder har etterlatt dusinvis døde i Benue og andre delstater. Kidnappinger og redningsaksjoner mot menneskehandel rapporteres også, mens regjeringen lover å redde bortførte barn i Borno.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
